newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Troubled Russian AvtoVAZ predicts higher 97 output.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Russian AvtoVAZ predicts higher 97 output.

text.p: Russia's heavily-indebted car maker AvtoVAZ revised slightly upwards its production forecasts on Friday and said car output would rise to 716,000 vehicles in 1997 from 680,570 in 1996.
The company's chief spokesman, Vladimir Isakov, said the company exported 132,000 cars last year, including 21,800 vehicles with General Motors electronic fuel injection systems.
Isakov had said in December 1996 that total 1997 output would be 701,000 cars.
The company has debts of about 10 trillion roubles ($1.8 billion).

AvtoVAZ is Russia's eighth biggest company by sales and its fifth biggest employer, but it has a tarnished management record, has been threatened by the government with bankruptcy and is struggling to transform itself.
